latin: अङ्गारेषु तथा भृष्ट्वा कालखण्डं विकृत्य च । पूगीफलप्रमाणेन खण्डान्कृत्वा विचक्षणः ॥ २ ॥ तैलेनाभ्यज्य तान्सर्वान्मरिचाजाजिसैन्धवैः । चूर्णितैर्विकिरेत्पश्चाद्धिङ्गुधूपेन धूपयेत् ॥ ३ ॥ अनेन विधिना भृष्ट्वा राजिकाकल्कलेपितान् । कालखण्डान्प्रकुर्वीत दध्ना राजिकयाऽथवा ॥ ४ ॥ भृष्टस्य कालखण्डस्य कृत्वा चक्कलिकाः शुभाः । केसरैर्मातुलिङ्गस्य सैन्धवाद्यैश्च मिश्रयेत् ॥ ५ ॥ समेदस्कौ द्विधा भक्तौ कृत्वा लवणमिश्रितौ । आम्लकैर्भावयित्वा तौ तैलेन परिपाचयेत् ॥ ६ ॥
english: Having likewise roasted the *kālakhaṇḍa* [the liver] on embers and cut it up, the discerning cook, having made pieces of the measure of an areca nut [the areca nut is the size standard, not the material; the material, *kālakhaṇḍa*, is named in the preceding pāda and left out of the formula itself], should anoint them all with oil and scatter over them pepper, *ajājī* [cumin], and rock salt, powdered; afterwards he should fumigate them with asafoetida smoke. Having roasted them by this same method, he should make the *kālakhaṇḍa*s smeared with a paste of *rājikā* [black mustard] — or else with curd and *rājikā*. Of the roasted *kālakhaṇḍa* he should make fine *cakkalikā*s [thin slices of the shape described at 1436] and mix them with the *kesara* [pulp and filaments] of the citron and with rock salt and the rest. The two fat-covered ones [*samedaskau*: the verse is in the dual throughout — *samedaskau*, *bhaktau*, *miśritau*, *tau* — so a natural pair, most probably the two kidneys, which 1425 names in the dual, *vṛkkau*, immediately beside the *kālakhaṇḍa*], each having been divided in two and mixed with salt, he should steep in sour liquids and then cook right through in oil.

latin: क्रोडदेशोद्भवं मांसमंस्या सह विखण्डितम् । अंसकीकससंयुक्तं पार्श्वकुल्या समन्वितम् ॥ ७ ॥ मृद्भाण्डे स्थालवक्त्रे तन्निक्षिप्य बहलोदके । हिङ्गुना चार्द्रकेणापि सैन्धवेन च संयुतम् ॥ ८ ॥ काथयेत्सुचिरं कालं यावत्तन्मार्दवं भजेत् । उत्क्वाथितमिदं सूपं ख्यातं शास्त्रविशारदैः ॥ ९ ॥
english: Flesh arising from the chest region, cut up together with the shoulder, joined with the shoulder bone [*aṃsa-kīkasa*] and accompanied by the *pārśva-kulyā* [the "channel of the flank", i.e. the rack of ribs]: having put it into an earthen vessel whose mouth is a dish [*sthāla-vaktra*, a plate set over the pot's mouth as a lid], in abundant water, together with asafoetida, with fresh ginger, and with rock salt, he should decoct it for a very long time, until it attains tenderness. This soup is called *utkvāthita* ["boiled right up"] by those skilled in the treatises [ms D reads "by those skilled in the treatises on soups"].

latin: विशैस्तस्य च मेषस्य जठरं पाटयेदनु । आन्तरं सर्वमुत्सार्य बध्नीयादपराङ्घ्रिकौ ॥ १५१० ॥ शिरश्च रज्ज्वा दृढया ज्वालायां परितापयेत् । यावद्रोमाणि गच्छन्ति यावत्कृष्णत्वमेति च ॥ ११ ॥ ततः प्रक्षाल्य तोयेन शेषं क्रोडवदाचरेत् । अन्येषां श्वापदानां च शेषं मेषवदाचरेत् ॥ १२ ॥
english: And next one should split open the belly of that *viśais* sheep [1510a as printed, *viśais tasya*, is not a Sanskrit form, and the pāda was already corrupt in the manuscripts — ms D reads *cittalasya*; *viśastasya*, "of the slaughtered [sheep]", would fit both the sense and the metre], drive out everything within, and bind the two hind feet — and the head — with a stout rope, and scorch it all round in the flame, until the hairs are gone and until it turns black. Then, having washed it with water, he should proceed with the remainder as with the pig. And with the remainder of other wild beasts he should proceed as with the sheep.

latin: समेदस्कानि मांसानि कृत्वा दीर्घाणि कर्तनैः । हिङ्गुतोयेन संसिच्य लवणेन विलोडयेत् ॥ १३ ॥ छायायां तानि खण्डानि वायुना परिशोषयेत् । एकद्वित्रिदिनान्तेषु भृष्टान्यङ्गारपुञ्जके ॥ १४ ॥ स्थूलीकृतानि यावच्च स्वादुरुच्यानि यन्नृणाम् । उपखण्डकनामानि सर्वशाकोत्तमानि च ॥ १५ ॥ हरिणस्य तथा खण्डान् चक्कलीपरिकल्पितान् । सम्भारसहितान्प्राज्यलवणेन विमिश्रितान् ॥ १६ ॥ शोषितानपि चात्यर्थमग्निना परिभर्जितान् । हृद्यान्पथ्यान्सुगन्धांश्च कल्पयेदुपखण्डकान् ॥ १७ ॥
english: Having made fat-bearing meats long by cutting, he should sprinkle them with asafoetida-water and toss them about with salt. Those pieces he should dry right out in the shade, by means of the wind. At the end of one, two, or three days they are roasted in a heap of embers, until they are made thick, and tasty and appetizing to men. They bear the name *upakhaṇḍaka*, and they are the best of all *śāka*s [the side-dish class]. Likewise pieces of deer, fashioned into *cakkalī*s, provided with the seasonings, thoroughly mixed with abundant salt, and dried also exceedingly, then roasted all over with fire — such *upakhaṇḍaka*s he should prepare: pleasing to the heart, wholesome [*pathya*, the Ayurvedic dietetic category], and fragrant.

latin: रुरुशम्बरसारङ्गच्छागस्य नलकं पृथु । अग्नौ भृष्ट्वा शिलाघातैः स्फोटयित्वा प्रयत्नतः ॥ १८ ॥ मज्जानं तु ततो हृत्वा लवणाम्लेन हिङ्गुना । मरिचाजाजिचूर्णेन पचेत्स्थाल्यां विचक्षणः ॥ १९ ॥
english: The broad hollow bone [*nalaka*] of the *ruru* deer, the *śambara* [sambar], the *sāraṅga* [the spotted antelope; ms D reads *cittala*, also "spotted"], or the goat: having roasted it in the fire and carefully burst it open with blows of a stone, and having then drawn the marrow out of it, the discerning cook should cook it in a pot with salt and sour, with asafoetida, and with powdered pepper and *ajājī* [cumin].

latin: यस्य कस्यापि मेषादेः शिरो भृष्ट्वा विभिद्य च । आददीत च मस्तिष्कं काञ्जिकेन विपाचयेत् ॥ १५२० ॥ आणके तैलमध्ये वा यथारुचि पुनः पचेत् । चूर्णैः संयोज्य तत्पश्चाद्धिङ्गुधूपेन धूपयेत् ॥ २१ ॥
english: Having roasted and broken open the head of any animal whatever, beginning with the sheep, he should take out the brain and cook it right through with *kāñjika* [soured rice-water]. Then he should cook it again, as he likes, in an *āṇaka* [pan] or in the midst of oil. Having combined it with the powdered spices, he should afterwards fumigate it with asafoetida smoke.

latin: पक्षिणामपि सर्वेषां पिच्छानुत्सार्य सर्वतः । चञ्चुपादं पृथक्कृत्वा पाटयित्वा तथोदरम् ॥ २२ ॥ निष्कृष्यान्त्रादिकं सर्वं पूर्ववत्परिपाचयेत् । यथा सूकरमेषाणां क्रियाः प्रोक्ता विपाचने ॥ २३ ॥
english: For all birds as well: having driven off the feathers on every side, having separated beak and feet, and having likewise slit open the belly, having drawn out the entrails and all the rest, one should cook it right through as before — that is, as the operations have been declared for the cooking of pigs and sheep.

latin: सशल्कानां च मत्स्यानां शल्कं स्फोट्यं प्रयत्नतः । स्थूलाश्चेत्खण्डशः कार्याः लघवश्चेत्सरूपतः ॥ २४ ॥ मत्स्यानां छेदयेच्छीर्षं पुच्छं तेषां च पक्षिणाम् । विपाट्य जठरं तस्मादन्त्रकाण्यपसारयेत् ॥ २५ ॥ कह्लांकरोष्ट्र बडिशा दग्धा खवल चाचुकैः ? । पाठीनैश्च तथैतेषां पृथक् कृत्वा शिरः पचेत् ? ॥ २६ ॥ मत्स्यानां घर्षणं कार्यं तैलेन लवणेन च । यावत्पिच्छलतां याति मत्स्यगन्धश्च नश्यति ॥ २७ ॥ क्षालयेदुदकैः पश्चाद्धरिद्राकल्कमिश्रितैः । वस्त्रे बध्वा निपीड्यैतान् स्रावयेत्सङ्गतं जलम् ॥ २८ ॥ क्षिपेत्पूर्वप्रसिद्धेषु प्रपकेष्वाणकेषु तान् । स्वल्पे काले गते सूदः स्थालीमुत्तार्य धूपयेत् ॥ २९ ॥ मत्स्यखण्डानि धौतानि चिञ्चाम्लेन विपाचयेत् । ततो गोधूमचूर्णं तु विकिरेत्तेषु सर्वतः ॥ १५३० ॥ तप्ततैले क्षिपेत्तानि पिङ्गान्युत्तारयेत्ततः । एलामरिचचूर्णेन सैन्धवेन च भावयेत् ॥ ३१ ॥
english: Of fish that carry scales, the scales are to be knocked off with care. If they are large they are to be made into pieces; if small, [kept] in their own form. One should cut off the head of the fish, and the tail of those fin-bearers [*pakṣin*, "winged", used here of the fins]. Having slit the belly, he should draw the entrails out of it. *Kahlāṃ*, *karoṣṭra*, *baḍiśa*s, *dagdhā*, *khavala*, together with the *cācuka*s, and with the *pāṭhīna*s [the sheatfish, which carries no scales] likewise — of these, having separated the head, one should cook it. [Shrigondekar prints a question mark after each half-verse of 1526, marking the whole verse as doubtful, and records ms D's reading of the first pāda as *kandaṃ karoṣṭra biḍiśāḥ*. Both hemistichs scan at eight syllables, so no text is missing; the words are unidentified, and the construction of the second half requires them to be names of fish.] The fish are to be rubbed with oil and with salt, until [the fish] goes slimy and the fishy smell is destroyed. Afterwards he should wash them with waters mixed with turmeric paste; having tied them up in a cloth and pressed them, he should let the gathered water run off. He should throw them into the *prapaka*s and *āṇaka*s already made known [*prapaka* occurs nowhere else in the chapter and cannot be identified; *āṇaka* is the pan of 1521 and 1532]. When a little time has passed, the cook should take the pot off the fire and fumigate it. [Or] he should cook the washed fish pieces right through with tamarind sour; then he should scatter wheat flour over them on every side, throw them into heated oil, and take them out when they are tawny. He should finish them with powdered cardamom and pepper and with rock salt.

latin: आणके वा तथा तैले वह्नौ वा धूमवर्जिते । पूर्वोक्तविधिना मत्स्यान् यथारुचि विपाचयेत् ॥ ३२ ॥
english: Or in an *āṇaka* [pan], or likewise in oil, or on a fire free of smoke, one should cook fish by the method already stated, according to taste.
